mainTopic: Bringing the סוטה to be tested: the escort of תלמידי חכמים, רבי יהודה's view, and the court's efforts to make her confess
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: witnesses overseas are too rare to make people suspect innocent women. A new משנה then says the husband brings his wife to בית דין, which sends two תלמידי חכמים along so he is not with her on the way. רבי יהודה says the husband is trusted. The גמרא tries twice to prove rules of רב about יחוד from this משנה. Both proofs are turned aside: the two scholars are there to serve as witnesses, and they must be scholars because they know how to warn him. רבי יהודה's view rests on a קל וחומר from נדה. The רבנן turn it around, and the גמרא explains that after his קל וחומר was refuted he relied on a פסוק. A second משנה describes how the great בית דין in ירושלים presses the סוטה to confess. If she confesses, she loses her כתובה and is divorced. If she claims innocence, she is brought to שער ניקנור, where the כהן disgraces her by tearing her clothes and dressing her in black, and the משנה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Witnesses overseas would also cause suspicion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון. There is already a case where the water does not work: when there are witnesses overseas. That would also cast suspicion on innocent women.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the case where she has witnesses in a faraway country!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing an earlier discussion and attacks רבי שמעון's reasoning. Even by his view, the water sometimes fails to work, because there are witnesses who are far away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said זכות cannot hold back the water's effect, because then people would suspect innocent women who drank and were unharmed. The גמרא points out that a woman with witnesses overseas is also not tested by the water. So the same suspicion could arise anyway, and his reason seems weak.

keyTerms.meaning: A faraway country; literally 'a land across the sea'
The תנא whose view is being challenged here

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not part of the new משנה below. It closes the discussion from before about רבי שמעון and זכות.

phrases.english: There are witnesses for her in a country overseas!
phrases.notes: He means witnesses who saw her sin. When such witnesses exist, the water does not test her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier debate about רבי שמעון's view that זכות does not suspend the water.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's reason that זכות cannot suspend the water because it would defame innocent women
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Witnesses overseas already create a case where the water fails, so defamation would happen anyway.

steps.title: That case is rare
steps.stepSummary: Witnesses overseas are uncommon, so nobody will assume that is why the water did not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in two words. The overseas-witness case almost never happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People explain events by what is common. Having זכות is common, so people would use it to suspect a woman. Witnesses overseas are rare, so nobody will think of them, and innocent women stay protected.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not common; it rarely happens

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's concern is about what people will commonly assume. A rare case does not create suspicion.

phrases.english: It is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing by frequency: a rare case versus a common one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Witnesses overseas would cause the same suspicion as זכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only common explanations lead people to suspect a woman. The overseas case is too rare to matter.

steps.title: The husband brings her to court and gets two escorts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the first step. The husband takes his wife to the local בית דין, and the court gives him two תלמידי חכמים to travel with them. This is so he will not be intimate with her on the way.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he handle her? He brings her to the court in his town, and they assign him two Torah scholars, in case he would be intimate with her on the way.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It explains how the husband brings his suspected wife to be tested, with two scholars escorting them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While she is a סוטה, she is forbidden to her husband until she is tested. Being intimate with her would also stop the water from testing her properly. So בית דין sends two scholars along as guards on the trip.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה; the core teaching the גמרא will discuss

phrases.english: MISHNA:
What does he do with her?
phrases.notes: "He" is the husband, after she was secluded with the man he had warned her about.

phrases.english: He brings her to the court that is in that place,
and they assign him two Torah scholars,
lest he have relations with her on the way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about the procedure for testing a סוטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband brings her to the local בית דין, which sends two תלמידי חכמים along to make sure he is not intimate with her on the way.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the husband is trusted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees. The husband can be trusted not to be with her, so no escorts are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Her husband is trusted with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second opinion. רבי יהודה says there is no need for scholars to escort them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion worries the husband might give in on the road. רבי יהודה says we rely on the husband himself to keep away from her until the test.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Her husband is trusted with regard to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה about needing escorts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No escorts are needed, because the husband is trusted.

steps.title: Three men on the road: support for רב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא counts two scholars plus the husband, which makes three men. It suggests this supports רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two plus him makes three. Shall we say this supports רב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an observation about the משנה: there will be three men with her. It suggests this backs up רב's opinion, which it quotes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why did the משנה need two scholars and not just one? The גמרא assumes the escorts are there to avoid יחוד. If so, the משנה wants three men on the road, which fits רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Shall we say it supports him? This introduces a suggested proof.

steps.confusionAlert: "לֵימָא" ("shall we say") is only a suggestion. The גמרא is testing whether the proof works, not announcing that it does.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Two and he,
phrases.notes: "Two" means the two scholars, and "he" is the husband.

phrases.english: that makes three.
Let us say this supports Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the משנה's requirement of two escorts.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that on the road a woman needs three men with her
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's two scholars plus the husband, which makes three men on the trip

steps.title: רב's rule: three men are needed on the road
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that two men with a woman avoid יחוד only in town. On the road there must be three, since one may step away to relieve himself and leave the other alone with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The rule that two men are enough applies only in town. On the road you need three, because one may need to relieve himself, and then the other is left alone with a forbidden woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב's statement, which the משנה is said to support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In town, two men with a woman is enough to avoid יחוד. On a trip, one man may walk off for privacy and leave the other alone with her. So רב requires a third man.

keyTerms.meaning: רב יהודה quoting his teacher רב
They only taught this in the case of; this limits an earlier rule
Is alone with; this is the יחוד prohibition

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical יחוד rule: more people are needed on the road than in town.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
They taught this only in the town,
phrases.notes: "This" is the rule that a woman may be with two men, which is taught in קידושין 80b.

phrases.english: but on the road, not unless there are three,
lest one of them need to relieve himself,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן מִתְיַיחֵד עִם הָעֶרְוָה.
phrases.english: and it will turn out that one of them is alone with a forbidden woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the statement of רב that step 5 suggested the משנה supports.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In town, two men with a woman avoid יחוד. On the road, three are needed.

steps.title: The two scholars are there to be witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof for רב. The משנה sends two scholars so there will be two witnesses against the husband, not to prevent יחוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Here this is the reason: so that there will be witnesses regarding her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 5. The משנה sends two scholars, but not because of רב's rule about three men on the road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 counted husband plus two scholars as three men and saw support for רב. The answer is that the second scholar has a different job. If the husband is intimate with her on the way, there will be two עדים to testify, and testimony needs two. So the משנה tells us nothing about how many men are needed to avoid יחוד.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying יחוד does not matter here. It only says the count of two scholars has a different reason, so it cannot prove רב's rule of three.

phrases.english: No: here, this is the reason:
so that there will be witnesses regarding her.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא: הָכָא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלִיהְווֹ עֲלֵיהּ סָהֲדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in Step 5 for רב's rule quoted in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה for רב's rule of three men on the road.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The number two comes from the need for two witnesses, not from the rules of יחוד.

steps.title: Only scholars: support for another rule of רב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה specifies scholars and not just anyone. It suggests this supports a different statement of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Torah scholars, yes; anyone else, no. Shall we say this supports the other statement of רב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a new inference from the word 'scholars' in the משנה. It is setting up a second statement of רב, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have said 'two men,' but it said 'two תלמידי חכמים.' The גמרא suggests this detail matters. Perhaps only men of good character can protect a woman from יחוד.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say this supports him

phrases.english: Torah scholars, yes;
anyone else, no.
Shall we say this supports the other statement of Rav,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof for רב was rejected, the גמרא tries a new proof from a different detail of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that two men protect against יחוד only if they are decent men.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה specifies תלמידי חכמים rather than any two men.

steps.title: רב: two men only help if they are decent
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that two men with a woman avoid יחוד only when they are decent. With immoral men, even ten are not enough, as a real incident showed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: They only taught this about decent men. With men of loose morals, even ten are not enough. There was an incident where ten men carried a woman out on a bier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the statement of רב that the משנה might support. Two men only protect a woman from יחוד if they are decent people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is that a woman may be with two men. רב limits this to men of good character. With immoral men, numbers do not help, because they may join together to sin. The story of ten men carrying her on a bier shows that even a large group can cooperate in wrongdoing.

keyTerms.meaning: bier, a bed for carrying the dead

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule matters in practice for יחוד. Being in a group only helps when the people in it can be trusted.

phrases.english: as Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
They only taught this about decent men,
but with men of loose morals,
even ten are also not enough.
There was an incident
and ten men carried her out on a bier.
phrases.notes: They carried her out as if she had died, as a cover, and sinned with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא כְּשֵׁרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the statement of רב that Step 8 said the משנה might support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two men protect against יחוד only if they are decent. With immoral men, even ten do not.

steps.title: Scholars are needed because they know how to warn him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second proof. Scholars are chosen because they know how to warn the husband properly, not because ordinary men would fail to prevent יחוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Here this is the reason: because they know how to warn him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 8. There is another reason the משנה wants scholars specifically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scholars know the law. They know how to give a proper warning (התראה) to the husband if he tries to be with her. Ordinary men might not know how to do this. So the word 'scholars' does not prove רב's rule about decent men.
steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs for רב from this משנה fail. The two scholars serve as two witnesses, and they are scholars so they know how to warn the husband properly.

phrases.english: No, here this is the reason:
because they know how to warn him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, הָכָא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּיָדְעִי לְאַתְרוֹיֵי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof suggested in Step 8 for רב's rule in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the word 'scholars' for רב's rule about decent men.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Scholars are needed for their legal knowledge, so they can give a proper warning. Their good character is not the point.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's קל וחומר: the husband can be trusted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives רבי יהודה's reason. A husband is trusted alone with his wife when she is a נדה, which carries כרת. So surely he is trusted with a סוטה, which is only a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Her husband, etc. It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, her husband is trusted, from a קל וחומר. If with a נדה, who is forbidden under כרת, her husband is trusted with her, then with a סוטה, who is forbidden only by a לאו, is it not all the more so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי יהודה's view in the משנה (Step 4). It brings a ברייתא that explains his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband may be alone with his wife when she is a נדה, even though relations then carry the severe punishment of כרת. A סוטה is forbidden to her husband only by a לאו, which is less severe. If he is trusted in the more severe case, he is surely trusted in the lighter one, so no escorts are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: an argument from a more severe case to a lighter one
a woman in her menstrual state
it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the basis of the disagreement. The רבנן want escorts, while רבי יהודה relies on the husband's proven trustworthiness in a more severe case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Her husband, etc.
It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says,
her husband is trusted, from a kal vachomer:
If a niddah, who is forbidden under karet,
her husband is trusted with her,
phrases.notes: He is allowed to be alone with her during that time.

phrases.english: then a sotah, who is forbidden only by a lav,
is it not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בַּעְלָהּ נֶאֱמָן מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about רב, the גמרא returns to רבי יהודה's view in the משנה and gives its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband is trusted alone with a סוטה, by a קל וחומר from a נדה.

steps.title: The רבנן turn the argument around
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say the same comparison proves the opposite. כרת is serious, so the husband is careful with a נדה. A לאו is lighter, so he cannot be trusted with a סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: that very point proves the opposite. A נדה carries כרת, so it feels serious to him, and he is trusted. A סוטה is only a לאו, so it does not feel serious to him, and he is not trusted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's answer to רבי יהודה. They use the exact same facts to reach the opposite conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reasoned that if a husband is trusted with the more serious ban (נדה), he is surely trusted with the lighter one (סוטה). The רבנן say the seriousness is the very reason he is trusted with a נדה. A lighter ban like סוטה does not hold him back, so scholars must go with him.

keyTerms.meaning: That very point gives the reverse: the same reasoning leads to the opposite conclusion
A woman in her monthly impurity, forbidden to her husband
Spiritual cutting off, a very severe punishment
It is serious in his eyes

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree on the facts: נדה is כרת and סוטה is a לאו. They only argue about what those facts prove.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: that very point proves the opposite:
phrases.notes: Literally, 'it is what gives': the same reasoning gives the other side's answer.

phrases.english: A נדה, which carries כרת,
is serious to him, and so he is trusted.
A סוטה, which is only a לאו,
is not serious to him, and so he is not trusted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's counter-reasoning to רבי יהודה's קל וחומר from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because a סוטה is only a לאו, the husband does not treat it as serious, so he is not trusted alone with her.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה learn this from a verse instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבי יהודה uses a קל וחומר. It quotes a ברייתא that seems to show he learns the law from the פסוק 'the man shall bring his wife'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really learn this from a קל וחומר? But he learns it from the verses! As a ברייתא teaches: 'And the man shall bring his wife to the כהן.' By Torah law the man brings his wife himself. But the Sages said: we give him two Torah scholars to go with him, in case he is with her on the way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the ברייתא from step 11. Another ברייתא suggests רבי יהודה learns this law from a פסוק, not from a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new ברייתא first gives an unnamed view: by Torah law the husband brings his wife alone, based on the פסוק. The scholars are only a rule of the חכמים. The קל וחומר appears in this ברייתא under רבי יוסי's name instead, so it is hard to say it is רבי יהודה's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: He brings it from verses (learns it from the פסוקים)
They hand over to him (assign to go with him)
Lest he have relations with her

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר מַיְיתֵי לַהּ?
phrases.english: And does רבי יהודה derive it from a קל וחומר?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִקְּרָאֵי מַיְיתֵי לַהּ!
phrases.english: But רבי יהודה derives it from verses!
As it was taught in a ברייתא:
"And the man shall bring his wife to the כהן."

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַתּוֹרָה הָאִישׁ מֵבִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: By Torah law, the man brings his wife himself,
phrases.notes: This is the first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא. רבי יהודה's own words come at the end, in Step 16.

phrases.english: but the Sages said:
they give him two Torah scholars to go with him,
in case he is with her on the way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר מַיְיתֵי לַהּ? וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִקְּרָאֵי מַיְיתֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source attributed to רבי יהודה in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא in step 11 that gives רבי יהודה's reason as a קל וחומר from נדה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a different ברייתא, רבי יהודה himself learns the law from the פסוק 'וְהֵבִיא הָאִישׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ', not from a קל וחומר.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's קל וחומר from נדה
steps.stepSummary: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי יוסי says the husband is trusted, because of a קל וחומר: if he is trusted with a נדה, which carries כרת, he is surely trusted with a סוטה, which is only a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: her husband is trusted with her, from a קל וחומר. If a husband is trusted with a נדה, who is forbidden under כרת, then with a סוטה, who is forbidden only by a לאו, isn't he trusted all the more?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי יוסי's opinion. This is the same קל וחומר that step 11 gave as רבי יהודה's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, the קל וחומר from נדה is said by רבי יוסי. The ברייתא will soon quote רבי יהודה separately (Step 16), and there he relies on a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Trusted regarding her (trusted to be alone with her)
A 'how much more so' argument, from a lighter case to a stricter one
Is it not all the more so?

phrases.english: רבי יוסי says:
Her husband is trusted with her, from a קל וחומר:
If with a נדה, who is forbidden under כרת,
her husband is trusted with her,
then with a סוטה, who is forbidden only by a לאו,
isn't it all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, בַּעְלָהּ נֶאֱמָן עָלֶיהָ מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 13 with the second opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: the husband is trusted alone with his wife who is a סוטה, from a קל וחומר from נדה.

steps.title: The חכמים reject רבי יוסי's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say a נדה is different, because she will become permitted again. A סוטה may never become permitted, and forbidden things feel more tempting, as the פסוק 'stolen waters are sweet' shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: No. You can say that about a נדה, because she has a way to become permitted. Can you say the same about a סוטה, who has no way to become permitted? And the פסוק says: 'Stolen waters are sweet, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים in the ברייתא knock down רבי יוסי's קל וחומר. They point to a real difference between נדה and סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a נדה, the husband can wait, because she will soon be permitted again. With a סוטה, he may lose her forever, so the pull is much stronger. The פסוק from משלי shows that what is forbidden feels sweeter. This rejection is different from the רבנן's reason in step 12, which was about how serious the ban is.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (this is true in one case)
Will you say (the same in the other case)?
Stolen waters are sweet: forbidden things are more tempting

steps.whatToRemember: In this ברייתא the חכמים reject the קל וחומר from נדה, because a סוטה, unlike a נדה, may never become permitted. The ברייתא then quotes רבי יהודה citing a פסוק (Step 16), and Step 17 resolves the contradiction.

phrases.english: They said to him: No,
if you say this about a נדה,
that is because she has a way to become permitted;
will you say the same about a סוטה,
who has no way to become permitted?
And it says: "Stolen waters are sweet, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּנִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of רבי יוסי from step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יוסי's קל וחומר from נדה to סוטה completely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: נדה can become permitted again, so the husband can wait. סוטה may be forbidden forever, which makes the temptation stronger.

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns it from the verse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with רבי יהודה saying that by Torah law the husband brings his wife himself, based on the פסוק 'the man shall bring his wife'. This finishes the challenge from Step 13.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: By Torah law the man brings his wife to the כהן himself, as the פסוק says: 'Then the man shall bring his wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it began in Step 13. This last line is the whole point of the challenge: רבי יהודה learns the law from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (Step 11) we were told רבי יהודה's reason is a קל וחומר from נדה. Here the same רבי יהודה cites a פסוק instead. So which is his real source? The גמרא will answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law (as opposed to a rule added by the Sages)
'Then the man shall bring his wife': the פסוק about the סוטה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַתּוֹרָה הָאִישׁ מֵבִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ אֶל הַכֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: By Torah law, the man brings his wife to the priest,
phrases.notes: He means the husband brings her by himself, with no one sent along.

phrases.english: as it says: “Then the man shall bring his wife”!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מִן הַתּוֹרָה הָאִישׁ מֵבִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ אֶל הַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in Step 13, giving the line that creates the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 11 that רבי יהודה's source is a קל וחומר from נדה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this ברייתא רבי יהודה gives a פסוק as his source, not a קל וחומר, so the earlier report of his reason seems wrong.

steps.title: First the logic, then the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה first gave the קל וחומר. The חכמים knocked it down, so he then brought the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He first said the קל וחומר to them, and they refuted it. Then he said the פסוק to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: both reports are true, because רבי יהודה used both arguments, one after the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first argument was the קל וחומר from נדה (Step 11). It was refuted: Step 12 shows the רבנן answering it, and Step 15 shows a similar refutation of the same argument. Once his logic was refuted, he turned to a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: They refuted it (from פירכא, a refutation)

steps.whatToRemember: There is no contradiction. רבי יהודה started with a קל וחומר, and when it was refuted he brought a פסוק.

phrases.english: He said the קל וחומר to them first,
and they refuted it,
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't say which refutation. Step 12 shows the רבנן answering his קל וחומר, and Step 15 has a similar answer.

phrases.english: and then he said the verse to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ קַל וָחוֹמֶר בְּרֵישָׁא וּפַרְכוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 13 and 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Sequencing: both sources belong to רבי יהודה, said at different stages of the debate.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the two reports gave conflicting sources for רבי יהודה's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: He first used the קל וחומר. After it was refuted, he relied on the פסוק.

steps.title: Isn't רבי יהודה saying the same as the first opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה adds, since the תנא קמא of the ברייתא also seems to say this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יהודה's view sounds exactly like the first opinion in the ברייתא. So what is the argument?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two תנאים say the same thing, there is no reason to list them as separate opinions. The גמרא wants to find the real difference between them.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda is the same as the first tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling רבי יהודה's source, the גמרא asks how his view differs from the תנא קמא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Listing רבי יהודה as a separate opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His statement seems identical to the תנא קמא, so the ברייתא seems to repeat itself.

steps.title: They argue about the Sages' added rule
steps.stepSummary: The difference is the clause 'but the Sages said', which adds two תלמידי חכמים to go with the couple. The תנא קמא accepts it; רבי יהודה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the clause 'but the Sages said'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that they agree about Torah law but disagree about an extra rule the Sages added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says that by Torah law the husband brings her himself, 'but the Sages said' two תלמידי חכמים go along in case he is with her on the way. רבי יהודה says only the Torah law. He does not add the two scholars.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
'But they (the Sages) said': introduces a rule the Sages added

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא and רבי יהודה agree the Torah lets the husband bring her. They argue only about whether the Sages added two scholars to go with them.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
“But they said.”
phrases.notes: This points to the first opinion's line that the Sages send two Torah scholars along. רבי יהודה leaves that part out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a practical difference between the two opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יהודה and the תנא קמא held the same view.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ on the Sages' added rule of sending two scholars along.

steps.title: The new משנה: warning her in the great court
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. The סוטה is brought to the בית דין הגדול in ירושלים, where the judges warn her the way they warn witnesses in capital cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: They would bring her up to the great בית דין in ירושלים, and warn her strongly, the same way they warn witnesses in capital cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The discussion of the last משנה is done, and a new משנה starts. It describes the next stage: bringing the woman to the great בית דין and pressing her to admit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judges try to frighten her into confessing, so she will not drink the water and die if she is guilty. The משנה compares this to the serious warning given to witnesses in a case where a life is at stake.

keyTerms.meaning: The great court, the סנהדרין in ירושלים
They warn strongly, put fear into
Witnesses in capital cases, where a life is at stake

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the section about how the court tries to get the סוטה to confess before she drinks.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
They would bring her up
to the great court that was in Jerusalem,
and they would warn her strongly,
the way they warn witnesses in capital cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ מַעֲלִין אוֹתָהּ לְבֵית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of the previous one ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סוטה is brought to the great בית דין in ירושלים and strongly warned, like witnesses in capital cases.

steps.title: The judge gently explains why people slip
steps.stepSummary: The judge tells the סוטה that wine, joking around, immaturity and bad neighbors lead many people to sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: The judge says to her: My daughter, wine causes a lot, joking around causes a lot, immaturity causes a lot, and bad neighbors cause a lot.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues describing what the judge says to the סוטה. He speaks softly and gives her understanding reasons, so that it will be easier for her to admit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 had the judges warn her sternly, the way witnesses are warned. Here the tone changes to gentle. By listing reasons people slip, the judge makes confessing feel less shameful.

keyTerms.meaning: My daughter, a soft and caring way of addressing her

phrases.english: And he says to her: My daughter,
wine causes a lot,
phrases.notes: "Causes a lot" means it leads many people into this kind of sin.

phrases.english: joking around causes a lot,
immaturity causes a lot,
bad neighbors cause a lot.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר לָהּ: בִּתִּי, הַרְבֵּה יַיִן עוֹשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of how the judges speak to the סוטה, moving from a stern warning to gentle encouragement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The judge encourages her to confess by naming common causes that lead people to sin.

steps.title: Saving ה׳'s name and telling hard stories
steps.stepSummary: The judge asks her to confess so ה׳'s holy name will not be erased in the water. He also tells her things that are embarrassing for her and her family to hear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Act for the sake of His great name, which was written in holiness, so that it will not be erased on the water. And he says before her things that are not fit to be heard, by her and all her father's family.
steps.whatsHappening: The judge gives two more pushes to confess. He makes a spiritual appeal about ה׳'s name, and he tells her uncomfortable stories in front of her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Part of the סוטה process is erasing a scroll that contains ה׳'s name into the water. If she confesses, the scroll is never erased, so confessing protects ה׳'s name. The "things not fit to hear" are a further form of pressure.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of His great name

phrases.english: Act for the sake of His great name,
which was written in holiness,
so that it will not be erased on the water.
phrases.notes: The scroll with ה׳'s name gets erased into the water she drinks (במדבר 5:23).

phrases.english: And he says before her things
that are not fit to be heard,
by her and all her father's family.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two more ways the judge encourages her to confess.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The judge urges her to confess so ה׳'s name will not be erased, and he tells her difficult stories.

steps.title: If she admits, she loses her כתובה and leaves
steps.stepSummary: If she says she is טמאה, she gives up her כתובה money and is divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she says, "I am defiled," she breaks her כתובה and leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the first possible outcome. If she confesses, the process stops: she loses her כתובה and is divorced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her confession ends the case without the water. Because she admits to the sin, she gives up any claim to her כתובה payment.

keyTerms.meaning: "I am defiled", meaning an admission that she sinned
She gives up her כתובה, by writing a receipt for it
And she leaves, meaning she is divorced

phrases.english: If she says, "I am defiled,"
she breaks her כתובה and leaves.
phrases.notes: "Breaks" here means she writes a receipt giving up her כתובה money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the result if the judge's efforts lead her to confess.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוטה who confesses forfeits her כתובה and is divorced.

steps.title: If she claims innocence, she is brought to the Eastern Gate
steps.stepSummary: If she says she is pure, she is brought to the Eastern Gate by שער ניקנור. That is the place where סוטות drink, יולדות are purified, and מצורעים are purified.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if she says, "I am pure," they bring her up to the Eastern Gate at the entrance of שער ניקנור. There they give the סוטות the water to drink, purify women who gave birth, and purify the מצורעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second outcome. If she insists she is innocent, the process continues and she is brought to the Eastern Gate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names the exact spot, and it describes that spot as the place for three ceremonies: the סוטה drinking, the purification of a יולדת, and the purification of a מצורע.
steps.whatToRemember: Confession ends the case: she loses her כתובה and is divorced. Claiming innocence moves her forward to the Eastern Gate by שער ניקנור for the water.

keyTerms.meaning: "I am pure", meaning she claims she is innocent
The Gate of Nicanor in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: But if she says, "I am pure,"
they bring her up to the Eastern Gate
which is at the entrance of the Gate of Nicanor,
for there they give the sotah women the water to drink,
and they purify women who gave birth,
and they purify the lepers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite outcome from Step 23: she claims innocence instead of confessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוטה who claims innocence is brought to the Eastern Gate at שער ניקנור, the place where סוטות drink and יולדות and מצורעים are purified.

steps.title: The כהן pulls her clothes and loosens her hair
steps.stepSummary: The כהן grabs the סוטה's clothes and pulls without caring whether they rip, until her chest is uncovered. Then he loosens her braided hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן takes hold of her clothes. If they rip, so be it. If the seams come apart, so be it. He keeps pulling until her chest is uncovered, and then he loosens her hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the ceremony at the Eastern Gate. It describes how the כהן publicly disgraces the סוטה by uncovering her chest and undoing her hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'if they rip, they rip' show that the כהן makes no effort to protect her clothing. The goal is to shame her in public. Undoing her hair is a step toward the פסוק's instruction that the כהן loosen the hair of the woman's head.

keyTerms.meaning: they are torn (a rip in the cloth)
they come apart at the seams
undoes or loosens her braided hair

phrases.english: And the priest grabs hold of her clothing.
If they are torn, so they are torn.
And if the stitches come apart, so they come apart.
Until he reveals her heart.
phrases.notes: Literally 'her heart.' He means her chest area.

phrases.english: And he unbraids her hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ceremony after she is brought to the Eastern Gate by שער ניקנור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן pulls her clothes without concern for damage until her chest is uncovered, and he loosens her hair.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: Do not uncover her if she is attractive
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion. If her chest or hair is attractive, the כהן does not uncover her chest or loosen her hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if her chest was attractive, he would not uncover it. If her hair was attractive, he would not undo it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different opinion from the one just stated in the משנה. He limits when the כהן uncovers her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says the כהן always uncovers her chest and hair. רבי יהודה says this is not done when she is attractive. The משנה does not give his reason here.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not adding to the first opinion. He disagrees with it. In his view the uncovering sometimes does not happen at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה לִבָּהּ נָאֶה — לֹא הָיָה מְגַלֵּהוּ,
phrases.english: If her heart was attractive, he would not reveal it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הָיָה שְׂעָרָהּ נָאֶה — לֹא הָיָה סוֹתֵר.
phrases.english: And if her hair was attractive, he would not unbraid it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion's rule that the כהן always uncovers her chest and hair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, an attractive chest or attractive hair is not uncovered.

steps.title: Her white clothes are replaced with black, and gold jewelry is mentioned
steps.stepSummary: If the סוטה was wearing white clothing, the כהן covers her with black clothing instead. The משנה then begins a new rule about gold jewelry, which continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was dressed in white, he covers her with black. If she was wearing gold jewelry...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues describing how she is made to look unattractive. Her bright clothing is replaced with dark clothing. The line about gold jewelry is only the start of a sentence, and the משנה finishes it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: White clothing looks nice, so the כהן replaces it with black. This fits the theme of disgracing her in public. The gold jewelry case follows the same pattern, but its ruling comes in the next section.

phrases.english: If she was dressed in white garments, he covers her with black garments.
If she was wearing gold adornments,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main description of the ceremony after רבי יהודה's disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If her clothing is white, it is replaced with black. The rule for gold jewelry is still being set up.
